items.finalStem: A domestic basket costs 120 domestic currency units; a comparable foreign basket costs 150 foreign currency units. With e = 2 foreign currency units per domestic unit and ε = eP/P*, what is ε?
items.units: (foreign currency/domestic currency) × (domestic currency/domestic basket) / (foreign currency/foreign basket) = foreign baskets/domestic basket.
items.method: Independently substitute final-stem inputs into the selected identity before comparing options.
items.keyedOption: 1.60 foreign baskets per domestic basket

items.units: (foreign currency/domestic currency) × (domestic currency/domestic basket) / (foreign currency/foreign basket) = foreign baskets/domestic basket.
items.method: Independently substitute final-stem inputs into the selected identity before comparing options.

items.method: Independently substitute final-stem inputs into the selected identity before comparing options.

items.units: Crowns per instrument / USD per instrument = crowns/USD. Then (crowns/USD) × USD/crowns = comparable-basket ratio.

items.finalStem: In one period, consumption rises $96 billion, of which $72 billion is imported. Measured investment rises $35 billion, including $11 billion of imported equipment. items.method: Independently substitute final-stem inputs into the selected identity before comparing options.

items.finalStem: Two countries initially have S = $700 billion and I = $750 billion. In Alder, saving rises $65 billion while investment rises an unknown amount. In Brin, saving rises $40 billion and investment rises $25 billion. What condition makes Alder end with a smaller trade deficit than Brin but still a deficit?

items.method: Solve endB < initialNX+deltaSA-deltaIA < 0; exclude both boundaries.
items.keyedOption: Alder investment rises by more than $15 billion but less than $50 billion

items.finalStem: Initially NX and NCO are zero. Residents increase foreign-asset purchases by $126 billion. Exports then rise $54 billion and imports rise $18 billion. What change in foreign purchases of domestic assets reconciles both accounts, and what does it establish about the causal sequence?

items.finalStem: A deficit lowers public saving $74 billion. Private saving rises by an unknown amount, domestic investment falls $22 billion, and NX falls $31 billion. Which private-saving response and interpretation reconcile the accounts?

items.method: Independently substitute final-stem inputs into the selected identity before comparing options.

items.finalStem: The U.S. dollar buys 10 percent more euros but 5 percent fewer yen. From these bilateral changes alone, what follows about the euro price of one yen?

items.method: Independently substitute final-stem inputs into the selected identity before comparing options.

items.method: Independently substitute final-stem inputs into the selected identity before comparing options.

items.finalStem: An agency quotes £0.75 per U.S. dollar with no fee, then £0.84 per dollar with a 3 percent fee added to the converted dollar charge. A £420 booking keeps its pound price. What is the new dollar cost, and what fee rate would exactly eliminate the benefit of the better quote?
